purpose: Scenario-neutral authoring contract for an ordinary semantic candidate.

semantic_handoff.candidate_integrity: The candidate is one complete, self-contained, immutable semantic object; whole-candidate integrity applies to its meaning and content, not to one platform transaction.
semantic_handoff.protocol_translation: Protocol alone translates that immutable candidate into dependency-ordered platform stages.
semantic_handoff.stage_atomicity: Atomicity applies independently to each required apply stage: run dry_run, then apply_atomic for that stage.
semantic_handoff.receipt_binding: Protocol binds generated platform IDs and IRIs only from preceding formal receipts or required reads before dependent stages.
modeling_exclusions: Batch or Item IDs and envelopes

candidate_revision.rule: Always a lowercase safe identifier string sent as a JSON string; a full revision uses the next strictly greater such string. Integer revisions are valid only for the R2.3-003 existing-scope task, whose own instruction pins the positive-integer sequence.

consumer_query_required_paths.rule: Every consumer_query.semantic.required_paths element is exactly the local name of one predicate declared by a predicate item in the same candidate (for example neutralAssociation). A full path expression such as subject--predicate-->object or an IRI is invalid; an illegal retrieval plan is rejected before the receipt is built and requires one complete revised candidate.

shape_path_min_count.rule: A shape path that must be present on every instance declares min_count (for example 1); a path without min_count imposes no presence constraint. A negative_probe whose expected_result is rejected for a missing value must reference a shape path that declares min_count, otherwise the candidate is internally inconsistent and its own validation gates can never be satisfied after acceptance.

consumer_query_one_connected_binding.rule: Every predicate named in consumer_query.semantic.required_paths is instantiated by exactly one relation (or fact) item in the whole candidate - one subject-object pair - so the query resolves to exactly one connected binding. A predicate instantiated on two different pairs (for example one generic hasKnownGap relation per explicit unknown) is ambiguous and is rejected with consumer-query-plan-invalid on every revision that keeps it in required_paths. Keep multi-instance predicates out of required_paths; give each explicit unknown a dedicated single-instance predicate referenced by its own consumer_query item, and when one query lists several paths their unique bindings must share a connected subject.

closure_checklist: Keep candidate_revision a lowercase safe identifier string matching [a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,127}; never send it as a JSON number.
Keep every consumer_query required_paths element a bare predicate local name declared by a predicate item in the same candidate; never a full path expression or an IRI.

Keep every predicate named in consumer_query required_paths instantiated by exactly one relation (or fact) item - one subject-object pair - in the whole candidate; a predicate with two instances (for example a generic per-unknown predicate) never resolves and must be replaced by dedicated single-instance predicates.
Give every shape path that a negative_probe relies on for rejection an explicit min_count (for example 1); a path without min_count never rejects a missing value.
Keep semantic integrity whole-candidate and immutable; Protocol owns dependency-ordered platform translation, per-stage atomicity, and receipt-bound generated IDs/IRIs.

Keep candidate constraints semantic-only; do not put platform execution strategy, fresh Project/Ontology scope, Batch/Item envelopes, dry_run/apply_atomic commands, or a whole-candidate atomic-apply instruction into the candidate.
Keep every item_id unique and every item_kind non-empty; semantic must be an object.
For every entity or explicit_unknown item materialized as create_entity, semantic.values.label must be non-empty source-grounded semantic text.
When a negative_probe materializes semantic.invalid_instance for rejection, that invalid instance must also carry a non-empty source-grounded label.
Treat labels as semantic content; Protocol rejects missing or blank labels and never derives or invents them from item_id, entity_id, or question text.
Declare each fact predicate, relation predicate, Shape path, and negative-probe path once in the current candidate.
For an object-valued predicate with an approved formal range, give it exactly one declared target Class. Omit the range when no formal Class restriction is confirmed.

When a formal range is required for heterogeneous object targets, declare one common superclass with subclass bindings or split the predicate; never use resource or an external placeholder as a range.
Resolve every class, entity, predicate, relation, Shape, path, and probe reference from the current candidate only.
Keep Team Transport delivery/reply identities and Batch/platform IDs outside the neutral semantic candidate.

constraints: Every declared path is unique in this candidate.
Object targets resolve through the declared common superclass.

semantic.description: Common superclass for the two illustrative subject classes.

values.label: Unresolved neutral subject
values.unknownRationale: The illustrative evidence does not identify one.

field_rules.semantic_role: A non-empty business semantic role string. Common roles are object, behavior, rule, business_role, process, data_mapping, interface_mapping. They are declarations, not platform resource kinds, permission roles, fixed enums or view labels. Additional confirmed meanings such as classification/context/local_usage are allowed. Multi-view references do not change the declared role.
field_rules.business_meaning: Non-empty natural-language meaning, including responsibility or property value/unit/direction meaning as applicable.
field_rules.applicability: Non-empty natural-language business applicability. It never grants a platform permission or selects a graph/Ontology.
field_rules.unknowns: List of non-empty unresolved questions. [] explicitly declares no known unknowns in this delivered definition; omission declares no information.
field_rules.not_applicable: List of explicit non-applicable meanings; absence is not evidence of non-applicability.
field_rules.conflicting_meanings: List of known unresolved conflicting explanations; keep each rather than silently selecting one.

candidate_rules: Place semantic_definition within semantic on ordinary class, predicate or entity/explicit_unknown items. In unified graph candidates it is an optional item field; copy the approved declaration unchanged into the corresponding command payload.

Use one candidate definition identity once. References use its entity semantic ID or a relation endpoint wrapper {definition_ref: item_id} for a class, predicate or entity declaration in this complete candidate. Never merge by label or alias; different meanings require distinct identities.

An entity may omit class, or provide classes as a list of neutral Class IDs. This expresses formal membership only. When class and classes both appear, the scalar must be among the list. Ordinary grouping is a business predicate relation, never implicit formal membership.

Predicates may omit domain and object-valued range when no formal Class restriction is approved. A fact predicate retains its datatype range. A formal subclass is declared only for confirmed set inclusion.

A relation with different local meaning is represented by a separate ordinary semantic node carrying its local semantic_definition and explicit relations to context, shared definition, source, target, and predicate definition as needed. The defining predicates explain each link. Do not place semantic_definition on an anonymous relation item.
Keep local context references as ordinary graph relations, not hidden IRI strings inside semantic_definition. Local meanings do not overwrite shared declarations.

Protocol owns platform identity/receipt binding and dependency ordering. definition_ref is a current-candidate reference only; receipt-backed existing_entity_ref keeps its existing authorized task contract. No global registry or cross-Project sharing is introduced.

All fields are optional to preserve previous contracts. A v4 definition must declare confirmed role, meaning and scope needed by its consumer; unresolved parts are explicit unknowns. No Evidence or lineage fields are added.
multiview_semantic_definition.readback: Existing governed read models class-detail, entity-detail, ontology-schema-summary, property-list, relation-type-list and entity-list project detail_fields.semantic_definition. Exact /api/semantic/resources/{iri} projects it in properties.semantic_definition. Generic relation/statement reads expose context/reference links. Hidden resources follow the existing indistinguishable 404/empty result contract. Only authorized returned content supports a business interpretation.

parameter_definition.value_type: Non-empty confirmed value type string, or null for unknown.
parameter_definition.occurrence_condition: Non-empty result appearance condition, or null for unknown.
parameter_definition.unit: Non-empty confirmed unit, or null for unknown.
parameter_definition.enum_values: Scalar value array; [] means no declared enumeration restriction; null means unknown.
parameter_definition.missing_meaning: Non-empty confirmed missing-value meaning, or null for unknown.

annotation_rules: These are optional annotations on ordinary entity definitions, not new resource kinds. In neutral candidates place them inside semantic; in unified candidates use optional item fields. Protocol copies approved content unchanged into create/update_entity payloads.

Each annotation is a non-empty object, or null to clear it. Each listed field is optional. Omission means no information, never none or unknown. No defaults are inferred. Unknown fields or invalid values return a local repairable payload error.

Each Action declares semantic_definition.semantic_role=behavior, a label, meaning and scope. Manual or unconnected Actions never require an Operation, Class, tool binding, execution risk, credential or idempotency declaration.

Each input/output position is a separate ordinary entity with a label and semantic_definition meaning/scope. Keep different parameter identities even when they reference the same object type. Identity does not assert distinct runtime objects.

For confirmed parameter contracts declare direction, value_kind, cardinality and required or occurrence_condition; use unknown/null and semantic_definition.unknowns for unresolved parts. No actual parameter values or relational rows are materialized.

Outputs declare result_kind when confirmed. An updated_input result links to the specific input parameter through an ordinary relation. New-object and computed-value meanings are explicit; omission does not infer either.

None input/output status is an explicit absence declaration, defined points to declared parameters via ordinary relations, unknown preserves unresolved meaning. Missing output status does not mean no output. No return value does not mean no effect.
relation_rules: Define ordinary relation predicates with confirmed meanings. Link Action to applicable object/Class definitions, parameter definitions, conditions, effects, scoped responsibilities and capability association nodes. Examples of local predicate names: appliesTo, hasParameter, hasPrecondition, hasEffect, hasResponsibility, hasCapabilityAssociation; none is a platform built-in.

All resource references use ordinary graph edges, never JSON IRI strings in annotations. Neutral relation endpoints may use {definition_ref: item_id} to reference current-candidate class, predicate, entity or operation definitions. Existing-resource bindings retain their own authorized receipt contract.

Conditions and effects are ordinary nodes with semantic_definition role, natural-language meaning and applicability; link them to relevant parameters, properties, objects or shared rules. A successful effect uses explicit success scope. Known rejected/failed/partial outcomes and conflicting interpretations remain readable, never become already-occurred facts.

Formal subclass applicability follows the explicit rdfs:subClassOf path; preserve common preconditions and scoped additional conditions together. No override/exception priority or execution decision is inferred. A no-Class object remains legal. Scope exceptions explicitly or use a distinct confirmed Action meaning; keep known multiclass conflicts in conflicting_meanings.
Scoped responsibility nodes link the Action, shared role definition and applicable context. Such relations never grant reading or execution rights.

Capability association nodes record corresponding meaning, applicability, unknowns and conflicts in semantic_definition, and link to confirmed Operations. Zero/many associations are legal and reusable. Multiple links imply neither equivalence, alternative completeness nor ordering. A partial step describes its combination gap; no composition/selection engine is added.

Changing an association does not mutate the shared Action definition or establish compatibility. An actual semantic change must revise that definition. Do not copy Operation risk/idempotency/credentials/conditions/effects onto an Action without confirmation.

neutral_operation.identity: semantic.operation_id is a stable neutral identity; definition_ref uses the operation item_id.
neutral_operation.target: semantic.target_class names a Class in the candidate; Protocol translates it to target_resource_type_iri. Operation remains separate from ordinary Action/object definitions.
neutral_operation.validation: All remaining fields retain Operation v1 validation, including active binding requirements and prohibition of secrets. Protocol creates it after Class/property definitions, before association relations. No external call occurs.

reusable_action_semantics.readback: Existing entity-list/entity-detail expose detail_fields.action_definition and detail_fields.parameter_definition; exact resource reads expose the same fields in properties. Generic statements read Class/parameter/rule/Operation references including non-NamedIndividual endpoints. All use existing access filtering before pagination/counts. Hidden references are not copied into metadata; missing authorized links cannot establish absence. Operation semantics remain available through existing governed reads. No Evidence/lineage fields are added.

process_binding_semantics.representation: Ordinary entity, predicate and relation items; Class is optional. Names below are example model vocabulary, never reserved fields, resource kinds or execution commands.
process_binding_semantics.declarations: Put role, business_meaning, applicability and explicit unknowns/not_applicable/conflicting_meanings in semantic_definition. Reuse R4.0-003 parameter_definition on process parameters. All resource references are ordinary edges.

relations.invokesAction: Call site -> exactly one confirmed shared Action; not an occurred invocation.
relations.hasParameter: Action -> its own R4.0-003 parameter definition; direction is parameter_definition.direction.
relations.refersToDefinition: Parameter/value reference -> shared object/value meaning; not runtime object equality.
relations.forParameter: Input/output value reference -> specific parameter definition.
relations.outputOfCall: Output value reference -> specific call site, paired with forParameter for that Action output.
relations.toParameter: Binding -> input parameter of the invoked Action, or output parameter of the owning process.
relations.fromValue: Binding -> one source value reference; a collection is one explicitly collection-valued reference.
relations.baseValue: Property value reference -> base object value reference.
relations.viaProperty: Property value reference -> property/relation definition; declare direction and cardinality.
relations.guardedBy: Transition or binding -> local decision/shared rule; no platform evaluation.
relations.currentItemOf: Current item reference -> its own iteration scope.
relations.iterationResult: Loop-carried value definition -> this iteration update used next time.
relations.collectsValue: Result outside iteration -> specific iteration output reference.

facts.sourceKind: process_input, call_output, object_property, constant, iteration_item; a conversion or reduction instead explicitly references its own definition.
facts.selectionMode: Confirmed exclusive, priority or unknown choice; no implicit first edge/default on unknown guard.
facts.priority: Only confirmed business priority, never display order or implicit iteration order.
facts.conditionTiming: Confirmed pre or post condition for conditional repetition.
facts.literalValue: Approved semantic scalar constant only; declare its datatype and missing meaning.

authoring_checks: Each process, call, parameter, value reference, binding, transition and local scope has a stable independent identity. Multiple calls/processes reuse one Action and its parameter identities. Same Class/name or different IRIs do not assert runtime equality or inequality.

A complete input binding has one atCall, one toParameter belonging to that Action input, and one fromValue. A process output binding instead has atProcess and that process output. Parameter names, labels and paths never substitute for references.

A call output reference has both outputOfCall and forParameter, plus its iteration/branch scope and appearance condition when applicable. A property reference has baseValue and viaProperty with explicit direction/cardinality; multi-hop access uses separate references.

For every required input declare a source or explicit unknown; explain optional omission. Omitted/unknown/not-applicable/none/conditional output are distinct. No return value does not mean no effect. Unknown models may preserve known content but are not declared executable or binding-complete.

Declare entry, transitions and terminals separately from data dependencies. Each transition has one fromStep and one toStep. Preserve decision inputs, exclusive/priority selection, default and no-match consequences, or their unknowns. Alternative paths can converge without synchronization; conditional sources remain conditional.

Collection loops declare collection, current item, body and exit; nested current items link to separate scopes. Conditional loops declare pre/post timing, continuation, body and exit. One body-call definition represents any iteration; never duplicate runtime iterations.

Loop-carried references state initialValue, iterationResult and next-iteration meaning. Outside results state collection/selection/reduction semantics and link iteration output and rule. Zero iterations, empty collections, failed/missing output and ordering are confirmed or explicit unknowns; never invent last/first/default values.

A manual Action needs no Operation. Local implementation context links its business call, capability steps and confirmed order/dependencies. Each step retains Operation v1 requirements. API field/parameter mappings stay in R4.0-011; unresolved mappings are unknowns, never invented JSONPath or parameter IRIs.

Keep shared preconditions and local restrictions together; no silent waiver. Revise local bindings without overwriting shared Action/parameter declarations. Stable IRI is not compatibility proof; version binding and shared-change review remain R4.0-007.
Do not model parallel branches or all/any synchronization as sequential/exclusive paths: D8 excludes them this period. Disclose any such business requirement as a scope gap.

Do not save business rows, real arguments, credentials, execution state, Evidence or lineage. Approved semantic constants are definitions, not runtime values. Do not copy protected rule thresholds into public text/constants.
protocol_checks: Use the existing closed neutral/unified candidate fields. Neutral declarations belong in semantic; unified declarations remain approved optional item fields. Map values to ordinary properties, resolving declared fact predicates and datatypes; never add process_definition or a new command.

Modeling chooses semantics; Protocol preserves them and binds identities. Definitions precede reference relations. Business graph cycles are legal; no execution-order sort or flow reachability/dominance/termination validator is added. Existing shape/authorization/atomic-write constraints remain unchanged.

Invalid fields/types/duplicate identities/unresolved references return existing item/field-local repair feedback; correct and retry the same goal. A structurally legal wrong business binding can be stored: independent semantic acceptance must identify it, not a platform guess.

Read nodes via governed detail/list, edges and arbitrary facts via generic statements with existing paging/truncation status. Exact resource properties is a declared projection, not all fact predicates. Read non-NamedIndividual Class/property/Operation endpoints with statements. Do not infer order from returned rows.

The old consumer_query.required_paths contract requires one instance per listed predicate; repeated invokesAction/inScope are ordinary repeated vocabulary, not unique per-edge predicates. Use generic statement/relation reads; do not force them into that contract.

Hidden and nonexistent resources share existing 404/empty contracts. Filtering precedes paging/counts. Missing authorized edges prove neither no binding/guard nor a hidden resource; do not reveal hidden counts or convert authorization filtering into model unknowns.
Use existing Batch dry_run/apply_atomic, receipts and uncertain-write recovery. No process executor, new table/route, external invocation or authorization propagation is introduced.
process_binding_semantics.example_location: process_binding_example_candidate in the mounted platform-neutral-candidate-authoring.json; complete neutral candidate, not a unified-candidate envelope. For unified candidates preserve its meanings/references using the existing unified fields and approved materialization plan.
process_binding_semantics.verification_boundary: Functional fixture roundtrip proves contracts and storage/readback only. A12 real modeling and independent source-based semantic acceptance need separate authorization.
